name: Kerr-Newman Charged Rotating Black Hole
description: The most general stationary black hole solution, carrying mass, angular momentum, and electric charge. It unifies the Kerr and Reissner-Nordström metrics into a single electrovacuum spacetime.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ and $G$ explicit, and the parameters are the mass $M$, the spin per unit mass $a = J/(Mc)$, which carries dimensions of length, and the charge radius $r_Q$, fixed by $r_Q^2 = GQ^2/(4\pi\epsilon_0 c^4)$ from the total electric charge $Q$. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: By the middle of the 1960s two black hole solutions carried structure beyond bare mass. Kerr had just written down the rotating hole in 1963 [kerr1963], and the charged case without rotation had been known since the work of Hans Reissner and Gunnar Nordström in 1916 and 1918 [reissner1916, nordstrom1918]. The obvious remaining case, a hole that both spins and carries electric charge, fell almost immediately, and by an unexpected route. Ezra Newman and Allen Janis noticed that Kerr's metric could be conjured out of Schwarzschild's by a peculiar trick: shifting the radial coordinate into the complex plane and taking a particular slice [newman1965janis]. The maneuver had no rigorous justification, yet it worked.¶In 1965 Newman, together with five collaborators, applied the same complex shift to the charged Reissner-Nordström solution and obtained a metric describing a mass that is at once rotating and charged [newman1965kn]. His collaborators were E. Couch, K. Chinnapared, A. Exton, A. Prakash, and R. Torrence, all, like Newman, of the University of Pittsburgh [newman1965kn]. This is the Kerr-Newman solution. It contains every black hole metric that came before it: with the charge set to zero it returns to Kerr, with the spin switched off it becomes Reissner-Nordström, and with both it is Schwarzschild.¶Roy Kerr later recalled that Newman wrote down several real functions that might stand in for the charge term in Kerr's metric, gave them to his graduate students to test against the Einstein-Maxwell equations, and found that the simplest one worked [kerr2009]. In Kerr's view the method succeeded because all of these metrics have the Kerr-Schild form, and not because of any complex transformation [kerr2009]. Kerr also recalled that he and Alfred Schild had already charged the Kerr-Schild metrics before March 1964, and had announced only that the work with their student George Debney was continuing [kerr2009].¶Brandon Carter worked out the global structure of the family in 1968 and showed that every member without spherical symmetry contains closed timelike lines, and that when the charge or the spin is too large for a horizon the violation is as flagrant as it can be, any event joined to any other by a timelike line directed to the future [carter1968]. He also found a fourth constant of motion in the unexpected separability of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, so that the geodesics and the orbits of charged particles can be integrated completely [carter1968]. Demetrios Christodoulou and Remo Ruffini wrote the mass of a charged, rotating black hole in terms of its irreducible mass, its angular momentum, and its charge in 1971, and found that half the mass of an extreme charged hole can be converted into energy, against 29 percent for an extreme rotating one [christodoulou1971]. Charles Sheffield powered the ships of his McAndrew stories, from "Killing Vector" of 1978 on, with kernels, Kerr-Newman black holes whose rotational energy can be drawn off and whose charge lets them be moved about at will [sheffield1983mcandrew]. Óscar Dias, Mahdi Godazgar, and Jorge Santos gave strong numerical evidence in 2015 that Kerr-Newman black holes are linearly stable within Einstein-Maxwell theory up to 99.999 percent of extremality, finding no unstable mode in the full spectrum of their quasinormal modes [dias2015].¶Kerr-Newman is the most general stationary, asymptotically flat black hole in Einstein-Maxwell theory, and the uniqueness theorems make this precise: an isolated black hole at equilibrium is fixed completely by three numbers, namely its mass, its angular momentum, and its electric charge [carter1968]. Werner Israel proved the static cases in 1967 and 1968 [israel1967, israel1968], and Brandon Carter and Stephen Hawking carried the argument to rotating holes in 1971 and 1972 [carter1971, hawking1972]. David Robinson proved in 1975 that the Kerr family is the unique family of vacuum black holes with a horizon that is not degenerate [robinson1975], and Pawel Mazur settled the charged case in 1982, proving that the only exterior of a stationary, rotating electrovacuum black hole with such a horizon is Kerr-Newman [mazur1982].¶Whatever rich and complicated star collapsed to form it, the remnant remembers only these three. This is the content of the dictum that black holes have no hair [ruffini1971]. Gary Gibbons showed in 1975 that a charged black hole also loses its charge spontaneously by emitting particles [gibbons1975]. In the universe we observe, charge is quickly neutralized, so real black holes are described by Kerr, and Kerr-Newman matters for the theory of the family more than for astronomy.

related.text: Kerr-Newman with neither spin nor charge, $a = 0$ and $r_Q = 0$, where only the mass is left.
Kerr-Newman with the charge set to zero, $r_Q = 0$. Ezra Newman's group reached the charged metric by the complex shift that carries Schwarzschild's metric to Kerr's [newman1965janis, newman1965kn].
Kerr-Newman with the spin switched off, $a = 0$, a charged black hole that does not turn.
Kerr's black hole with a cosmological constant where this one has a charge. Carter found both in one family by asking the Hamilton-Jacobi equation to separate [carter1968separable].
The throat of the extreme hole with the charge switched off. With charge the throat slides toward the Bertotti-Robinson universe [bardeen1999].

Kerr-Newman is a Malament-Hogarth spacetime, as Gábor Etesi and István Németi noted in 2002 when they set a computer in orbit around Kerr's black hole and sent an observer in to the inner horizon [etesi2002].

The charged black hole of low energy string theory. Ashoke Sen set it spinning in 1992, which makes his solution string theory's counterpart of Kerr-Newman, with mass, charge, and angular momentum [sen1992].
With charge equal to mass, Kerr and Newman's metric is one spinning source of Israel, Wilson, and Perjés's fields, which hold any number of such sources in balance [hartle1972, perjes1971].

parameters.description: Spin per unit mass, $a = J/(Mc)$ with $J$ the angular momentum, carrying dimensions of length
Newton's constant, kept explicit along with $c$, so that the Schwarzschild radius appears throughout as $2GM/c^2$
Charge radius, $r_Q^2 = GQ^2/(4\pi\epsilon_0 c^4)$ with $Q$ the total electric charge, carrying dimensions of length; a horizon exists only for $a^2 + r_Q^2 \le G^2M^2/c^4$

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates of Robert Boyer and Richard Lindquist, $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time. The horizons are at $r_\pm = GM/c^2 \pm \sqrt{G^2M^2/c^4 - a^2 - r_Q^2}$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
